name: Lovable
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: Chat-based AI builder that turns prompts into full-stack web apps with built-in database, hosting, auth and payment connectors.
starting_paid_price: $25/month Pro (100 credits; about $21/month billed yearly), per third-party summaries of Lovable's pricing page
latest_funding: Series C, $400M at $13.3B valuation, 2026-08 (Menlo Ventures and EQT's Scaleup Europe Fund)
founders_or_ceo: Anton Osika (co-founder and CEO), Fabian Hedin (co-founder)
africa_presence_type: None found (community event and app-side Paystack connector only)
africa_evidence: No Lovable office, local pricing or local checkout found. A community-hosted 'SheBuilds x Lovable' day in Cape Town gave attendees free credits, and in Nov 2026 Lovable added a Paystack connector so apps built on Lovable can take card, bank transfer and mobile money payments in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa and Cote d'Ivoire; neither changes how Lovable itself is paid for.
availability_in_africa: Not found (Stripe says Lovable takes payments from customers in 150+ countries; no African country list found)
payment_methods: Stripe billing (cards plus Stripe-supported wallets and local methods; managed via the Stripe billing portal)
africa_use_case: Nigerian, Kenyan and South African founders, agencies and freelancers building client MVPs, school-fee and event-ticket apps would pay $25/month but often hit dollar-card limits on monthly renewals and credit top-ups.
notes: Largest independent vibe-coding platform (reported $600M+ annualised revenue, Sep 2026). Credit top-ups and auto top-up create frequent small card charges. The new Paystack app connector shows African builders are an audience Lovable already recognises, a useful opener. Stripe-powered checkout, so the pitch is adding Cozzipay as an alternative method.

name: Bolt.new
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: Browser-based AI agent (built on StackBlitz WebContainers) that prompts, runs, edits and deploys full-stack web and mobile apps, with Bolt Cloud hosting and databases.
latest_funding: Series B, $105.5M at about $700M valuation, 2025-01 (Emergence Capital and GV); about $135M total raised
founders_or_ceo: Eric Simons (co-founder and CEO), Albert Pai (co-founder)
public_contact_email: legal@stackblitz.com (legal notices only, published in StackBlitz terms)
africa_evidence: An events aggregator lists a past Lagos kickoff meetup for Bolt's World's Largest Hackathon and credits it to Bolt, but it was a local meetup for a global online hackathon, not an Africa-focused programme. No office, local pricing or local payment method found.
africa_use_case: Lagos and Nairobi developers and agencies prototyping fintech and commerce web apps would pay $18-25/month for Pro, and Bolt's token-based top-ups suit a prepaid local-currency wallet.
notes: Also sold through the Microsoft Marketplace for enterprise (since May 2026). Runs a Bolt Open Source Fund and helps community organisers host build events, which could be an angle for co-hosted African hackathons.

name: v0
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: Vercel's AI app builder that generates React/Next.js full-stack apps and agents from prompts, screenshots or Figma, deployable on Vercel.
starting_paid_price: $30/user/month Plus (includes $30 of monthly credits); older $20 Premium plan closed to new users
latest_funding: Not found for 2026 (parent Vercel; v0 not funded separately)
africa_presence_type: None found (one official community event in Lagos)
africa_evidence: A Luma listing describes Lagos's first official v0 in-person workshop as part of Vercel's global 'Prompt to Production' week. It was a single event in a worldwide series, with no office, local pricing or local payment method found.
payment_methods: Not found (billing is centralised on vercel.com; prices shown in USD excluding taxes)
africa_use_case: Frontend developers and design agencies in Lagos, Nairobi and Cape Town building Next.js sites for clients would pay $30/month, often alongside a Vercel Pro hosting bill on the same card.
notes: Owned by Vercel, so a Cozzipay deal would likely cover the whole Vercel billing account (v0 plus hosting). Higher entry price than peers. Vercel already runs community build weeks (Prompt to Production, Zero to Agent) that have included Lagos.

name: Replit
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: Cloud development platform whose Replit Agent builds, hosts and deploys full-stack apps from natural-language prompts.
starting_paid_price: $20/month Core (includes $20 of monthly credits; $18/month billed yearly)
latest_funding: Series D, $400M at $9B valuation, 2026-03 (led by Georgian)
africa_evidence: No Africa office, local pricing, local payment method or Africa programme found. A payments blog aimed at African users says Replit only accepts USD-capable cards with global payment support, and describes workarounds for failing local bank cards.
payment_methods: Cards (USD-capable cards per third-party guide); Google Pay reported working by users; PayPal not supported (Replit forum); card and ACH for Enterprise
africa_use_case: Students, bootcamp learners and indie developers across Nigeria, Ghana and Kenya who learn and ship on Replit would pay $20/month for Core and credit top-ups, but a public guide already documents their card failures.
notes: Strongest documented card-pain signal in this list. Recently expanding government business internationally (Middle East named) and partnered with Arabic.AI on free Arabic coding courses, which may interest North African users. Effort-based Agent billing means frequent top-ups.

name: Base44
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: All-in-one AI app builder that creates apps, websites, agents and backends from plain-language prompts, with database, auth and hosting included.
latest_funding: Acquired by Wix for $80M, 2025-06 (reported $200M ARR by Aug 2026)
africa_use_case: Non-technical SMB owners and consultants in Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa building internal tools, booking and inventory apps would pay $16-20/month on a self-serve plan.
notes: Owned by Wix, so procurement may route through Wix. Two credit meters (message and integration credits) that do not roll over. Also sold as an app in the Wix App Market.

name: Emergent
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
company: Agione Technologies Private Limited (operating as Emergent Labs)
hq_country: India (Bengaluru), with a US office in San Francisco
product: Agentic vibe-coding platform where AI agents build, test and publish full-stack web and mobile apps for founders and small businesses.
latest_funding: Series C, $130M at $1.5B valuation, 2026-07 (led by Creaegis; $230M total)
founders_or_ceo: Mukund Jha (co-founder and CEO), Madhav Jha (co-founder and CTO)
africa_evidence: No evidence found in searches. Emergent says it has users in 190+ countries, but no African office, local pricing, payment method or programme was found.
availability_in_africa: Not found (company reports users in 190+ countries)
africa_use_case: Small-business owners in Lagos, Accra and Nairobi (bakeries, salons, logistics) are exactly Emergent's stated non-coder SMB customer and would pay $17-20/month plus 50 credits/month per hosted app.
notes: SMB, non-developer focus matches Cozzipay's base. Every deployed app consumes credits monthly, so renewals are recurring. Indian company that has scaled to 200k+ paying customers in emerging markets, so may be open to local payment rails.

name: Rocket.new
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: AI app builder that produces production-ready web and mobile apps from prompts, bundled with market research and competitor-intelligence tools.
starting_paid_price: $25/month (100 credits that do not expire), per Rocket's own blog
latest_funding: Seed, $15M, 2025-09 (Salesforce Ventures and Accel, with Together Fund)
founders_or_ceo: Vishal Virani, Rahul Shingala, Deepak Dhanak (co-founders)
africa_evidence: No evidence found in searches. Rocket says 1.5 million people across 180 countries have tried it, with no African office, pricing or payment method found.
availability_in_africa: Not found (company reports users in 180 countries)
africa_use_case: African founders and dev shops building cross-platform MVPs and client apps would pay $25/month, and non-expiring credits suit irregular, prepaid spending.
notes: Moneycontrol reported a planned 2026 raise of $40-50M at about $500M valuation fell through after due-diligence concerns; worth checking stability before investing sales effort.

name: Anything
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: AI agent that builds and launches full mobile (iOS/Android) and web apps with design, backend, database, auth and payments included.
latest_funding: Series A, $11M at $100M valuation, 2025-09 (led by Footwork, with M13)
founders_or_ceo: Dhruv Amin (co-founder and CEO), Marcus Lowe (co-founder)
africa_use_case: African solo founders who want to launch and monetise mobile apps on the App Store and Play Store would pay $19-24/month.
notes: Sources conflict on the free tier: one review says building requires a paid plan, others list a limited free tier. Pricing page still lives on create.xyz.

name: Same.new
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: Browser AI builder that generates full-stack Next.js sites and web apps from chat prompts, screenshots or reference URLs (started as a website cloner).
latest_funding: Not found (Y Combinator W24 and Costanoa-backed)
africa_use_case: Freelance web designers in Nigeria and Kenya who rebuild client websites from reference designs would pay for a monthly plan.
notes: Docs say users can start building for free and cite 600k+ builders. Pricing page returned HTTP 429 during research, so the paid price is unconfirmed. Early 'clone any site' positioning may raise IP questions.

name: Hostinger Horizons (Hostinger AI Builder)
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: Hostinger's prompt-to-app builder (merged into Hostinger AI Builder in Aug 2026) that creates websites and web apps with hosting, backend and Stripe payments included.
starting_paid_price: $1.99/month Premium on a 48-month upfront term (renews at $10.99/month)
africa_evidence: Hostinger runs African storefronts that price in Nigerian naira (cards plus OPay), Egyptian pounds (cards, PayPal, Fawry) and Moroccan dirhams. Daba Finance reported Hostinger launched in Nigeria with AI tools and local-currency payments, and the Nigerian site promotes Horizons.
availability_in_africa: Available in most countries; Hostinger excludes only Belarus, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela. Dedicated storefronts for Nigeria (NGN), Egypt (EGP) and Morocco (MAD).
payment_methods: Varies by regional storefront. Global: cards, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, AliPay, crypto. Nigeria: Visa/Mastercard and OPay in NGN. Egypt: cards, PayPal, Fawry.
africa_use_case: Nigerian and Egyptian small businesses wanting a cheap AI-built site or booking app already pay in local currency, so the remaining gap is Kenya, Ghana and other markets without a local storefront.
notes: SWAP: replaces Firebase Studio (Google), which stopped new sign-ups on 2026-06-22 and sunsets on 2027-03-22. Hostinger already accepts local payments in Nigeria and Egypt, so pitch Cozzipay only for uncovered markets (e.g. Kenya, Ghana) or as an alternative to OPay. Low intro prices need long upfront terms.

name: Bubble
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: Visual full-stack no-code platform for web, iOS and Android apps, now with an AI agent and AI credits for generating and editing apps.
founders_or_ceo: Josh Haas and Emmanuel Straschnov (co-founders and co-CEOs)
africa_evidence: Bubble's expert directory lists an agency called No Code Africa, and forum threads show South African developers using Bubble. These are independent agencies and users, not a Bubble office, reseller or programme.
africa_use_case: African no-code agencies and startup founders running production marketplaces and fintech front ends on Bubble would pay $32-119/month per app, recurring for the life of the app.
notes: Mature, sticky per-app subscriptions (apps stay live only while paid). Bubble announced layoffs on 2026-11-17 and is restructuring around AI, so budgets may be tight. An existing African agency ecosystem could help with distribution.

name: FlutterFlow
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: Visual Flutter app builder (now FlutterFlow Studio) plus a new AI-native builder (Nov 2026) for native iOS and Android apps.
founders_or_ceo: Abel Mengistu and Alex Greaves (co-founders, former Google engineers)
africa_evidence: No office, local pricing or official programme found. The community forum has many Nigerian users, and directories list FlutterFlow agencies in Nigeria and Kenya, but these are independent users and firms.
payment_methods: Not found (prices exclude tax, which is added at checkout by location)
africa_use_case: Nigeria and Kenya have large Flutter developer communities and FlutterFlow agencies building mobile apps for local clients, who would pay $39-80/month per seat.
notes: Strong fit with Africa's mobile-first Flutter community. Runs Student Ambassador and independent Developer Group programmes; no African groups confirmed. Per-seat pricing grows with agency team size.

name: Softr
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: AI and no-code builder for business apps, client portals and internal tools on top of Airtable, Google Sheets, SQL and other data sources.
founders_or_ceo: Mariam Hakobyan (co-founder and CEO), Artur Mkrtchyan (co-founder and CTO)
africa_use_case: African NGOs, schools and SMEs building member portals and internal tools on spreadsheets would pay $19-25/month; Softr gives nonprofits and education groups 50% off.
notes: Pricing scales by number of app users, which suits small African teams. Business-ops buyer rather than developer.

name: Glide
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: GlideOS AI builder (launched Jun 2026) that turns spreadsheets, prompts or files into internal business apps, alongside the older Glide Classic no-code editor.
starting_paid_price: $25/month Basic (100 credits, GlideOS, monthly billing only)
africa_use_case: Field-operations teams in African SMEs, NGOs and agribusinesses that run on Google Sheets would pay $25-50/month for internal mobile apps.
notes: Two product lines with separate pricing (GlideOS and Glide Classic). Internal-tools buyer; GlideOS has no annual plans yet.

name: bilt.me
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: AI-native mobile app builder that turns prompts or Figma frames into native iOS and Android (React Native) apps with live preview and store publishing.
latest_funding: Pre-seed, EUR 615k (about $700k), 2026-09 (led by Superhero Capital; angels include Bolt and Lightyear founders)
africa_use_case: African product designers who work in Figma could turn designs into shippable mobile apps for local clients on a monthly plan.
notes: Very early (pre-seed); paid price not confirmed. Small team that may be open to a payments partnership, but revenue potential is small for now.

name: Tempo Labs
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: Collaborative AI development environment and visual editor for React apps that lets designers, PMs and engineers build and edit code together.
starting_paid_price: $30/month Pro (Mar 2026 review); another directory lists Pro from $50/month
latest_funding: Seed, $5M, 2025-10 (investors include Golden Ventures, Y Combinator, General Catalyst)
africa_use_case: React developers and product teams at African startups would pay a monthly Pro seat to speed up design-to-code work.
notes: Product appears to have moved toward a team workspace (issues, docs) plus a $4,500/month human-assisted Agent+ tier. Entry price unclear between sources.

name: Macaly
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
hq_country: Czech Republic (parent team.blue is in Belgium)
product: Prompt-first AI website and web-app builder with hosting, database, auth and SEO, plus Macaly Cloud for publishing apps built in Claude or ChatGPT.
africa_use_case: Small African businesses (florists, guesthouses, clinics) wanting a cheap AI-built website on their own domain would pay $10/month.
notes: Low price point suits African SMBs. Owned by European hosting group team.blue, which focuses on European SMEs, so a deal may need group-level approval.

name: Zoho Creator
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: AI-powered low-code platform whose CoCreator (Zia) generates business apps from a prompt or requirements document, with web and native mobile apps.
africa_evidence: Zoho opened an African office in Cape Town and later a second South African office. Zoho's Kenya page advertises pricing in Kenyan shillings and a local Kenyan support team, and Zoho's Nigeria country manager described naira pricing for Zoho One, which includes Creator.
availability_in_africa: Zoho markets to South Africa, Kenya and Nigeria with local teams; Kenya page states KES pricing.
africa_use_case: Mid-sized African firms already on Zoho One would use Creator for internal apps; local pricing exists, so Cozzipay's value would be one-click wallet payment rather than currency access.
notes: SWAP: replaces Mocha (getmocha.com), which shut down on 2026-08-01. Africa evidence is Zoho company-wide (Zoho is the vendor, not a holding parent); no Creator-specific KES/ZAR price page was confirmed. Zoho also runs a .KE domain partnership in Kenya giving Zoho One wallet credits. Low priority for Cozzipay since local billing already exists.

name: Dyad
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: Free, open-source desktop AI app builder that runs locally, works with your own API keys or local models, and keeps code on your machine.
africa_use_case: Cost-conscious African developers on unreliable connections can use Dyad offline with local models and upgrade to $20/month Pro to skip managing foreign API-key billing.
notes: Free open-source core and bring-your-own-key model reduce paid conversion. Pro is the only Cozzipay revenue line. Small indie company.

name: Vibecode
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: AI app builder (including an iPhone app) that builds web and native mobile apps and can sign and submit Swift iOS apps to the App Store from cloud Macs.
founders_or_ceo: Ansh Nanda (co-founder and CEO), Kehan Zhang and Riley Brown (co-founders)
africa_evidence: No evidence found in searches. (VibeCode Africa, a nonprofit AI-literacy community, is unrelated to this company.)
africa_use_case: African creators without a Mac who want to publish iPhone apps could use Vibecode's cloud build and pay $20/month, alongside the $99/year Apple developer fee that also needs a card.
notes: Removes the need for a Mac, a real barrier for African builders. Code export only from the $50/month Pro plan.

name: Rork
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: AI platform that builds native iOS and Android apps from natural language and helps creators launch and monetise them on the app stores.
starting_paid_price: $20/month Pro (100 credits), per Oct 2026 review; another source lists $29/month
africa_use_case: Aspiring app-store entrepreneurs in Nigeria, Kenya and Egypt building niche consumer apps would pay a monthly plan, with credits also covering simulator minutes and iOS builds.
notes: Free plan only designs screens, so builders must pay to ship. Pricing differs between sources.

name: a0.dev
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: AI mobile app builder that generates React Native (Expo) apps from chat and publishes them to the App Store and Google Play in one click.
africa_use_case: Mobile-first African developers shipping Android apps for local markets would pay $20/month to skip native build setup.
notes: Small YC startup; pricing page does not show prices in plain text, so the $20 figure is from reviews. A third-party traffic tracker reported a 27% traffic drop in mid-2026.

name: Blink.new
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: Full-stack AI app builder for founders that ships web and native mobile apps with database, logins, Stripe billing and hosting included.
africa_use_case: African solo SaaS founders who need auth, billing and hosting in one place would pay $25/month.
notes: Early-stage, founder-led and localised into several languages, so likely quick to decide. Built-in billing for users' apps is Stripe-based, which could also open a Cozzipay integration angle for apps built on Blink.

name: Readdy
category: AI app builders and vibe coding
product: AI website builder that generates complete multi-page sites with backend, database and login from text, screenshots, URLs or templates.
starting_paid_price: $25/month Starter ($15/month billed yearly), per Readdy's own blog
africa_use_case: African web-design freelancers and agencies serving SMB clients could use Readdy's agency and white-label tiers and pay monthly.
notes: Has agency and white-label plans ($72-199/month) that suit African digital agencies. Third-party price listings conflict (some cite $15 Starter monthly); company HQ not confirmed.
